anchors: must ask `check-ignore` about the FILE, not only the folder it goes in
decision: Code relying on git ignoring a file it writes asks check-ignore about the file as well as its folder, in one --stdin -z -v call with core.quotePath=false, reads each record's pattern and source (a ! pattern re-includes; a source outside the work tree is a per-user excludesFile), and asks ls-files separately about what is already tracked.

evidence.text: git 2.53.0 scratch repo with configs/* plus !configs/*.xml: check-ignore -- configs/ rc 0; check-ignore -v on configs/config-x.xml printed the !configs/*.xml rule with rc 0, plain check-ignore rc 1; git add -A -n staged configs/config-x.xml; -z without --stdin rc 128; without quotePath=false a non-ASCII name came back quoted; an excludesFile match printed its absolute path as the source.

reopen_if: git stops reporting a folder as ignored when a negation re-includes some of its files, or check-ignore -v stops printing negation matches.
why: A folder-level check exits 0 while a negation such as !configs/*.xml re-includes a file written into it, so git add -A stages the file the check called ignored; under -v a negation match also exits 0, so the exit code alone misleads.

anchors: refuses over a dirty file whose content is already the incoming one
decision: When git merge --ff-only refuses over a dirty file, fetch and compare git hash-object FILE with git rev-parse origin/main:FILE; if equal, checkout the file, fast-forward and re-check; never stash a peer's edit for this.

evidence.text: Probed in a scratch repo (ff_probe.sh): ff-only refused with the worktree file byte-identical to the incoming blob; checkout plus ff left the same bytes.

reopen_if: git merge --ff-only starts accepting a dirty file whose content equals the incoming blob.
why: Stashing a peer's identical edit in a shared checkout to get past the refusal risks losing or misplacing it.

anchors: Splitting a finished change into several commits by hunk
decision: Build earlier commits of a split as the final tree minus the later hunks with git apply -R of default-context hunks, never from -U0 hunks with --unidiff-zero, and test every commit alone.

evidence.text: Reported from a real split on 2026-11-19 (contrib queue entry, inherited); not reproduced here.

reopen_if: git apply --unidiff-zero gains ordering for insertions at a shared point.
why: Zero-context hunks are placed by line number alone, so two insertions at one point can land in the wrong order and an earlier commit fails to parse while the final tree is fine.

anchors: ### A repo that stores CRLF blobs on purpose
decision: In a repo whose blobs hold CRLF, never rewrite a tracked file in text mode; once an LF blob is in the index, re-adding a CRLF file normalises it again, so store the exact bytes with hash-object --no-filters -w plus update-index --cacheinfo and check git diff --cached --stat HEAD.

evidence.text: Probed in a scratch repo (crlf_probe.sh) under text=auto eol=crlf: after an LF blob was staged, git add of the restored CRLF file kept the whole-file diff; the hash-object --no-filters route showed one line.

reopen_if: git add stops normalising CRLF once the index blob is LF.
why: A one-word fix became a whole-file diff, and restoring CRLF plus git add did not repair it.
